talk_track: I spent last year turning a roofing-contractor SaaS from a pre-AI SDLC into an AI-native one: cycle time went from 42 hours to under 20, merged PRs per developer up 115%, mobile release time down 98%. Your open Software Engineer role says Hauler Hero is "embracing AI-assisted development as a core part of how we build software" and wants engineers with 2-4 years of experience to master those tools early. Here is what that posting actually commits you to, from having done it: AI does not remove the bottleneck, it moves it — engineers become code auditors, and review and discovery become the new constraint, which lands hardest on the least experienced people on the team. The teams that keep the gains instrument cycle time and PR throughput before they scale AI usage, not after, because otherwise you cannot tell a real speedup from more code arriving faster. That is worth knowing whether or not you ever reply. Do you have a cycle-time baseline yet? — Bill Bowers
